patterns.title: Story-anchored openings
patterns.observation: Both top vlogs open mid-scene with a date and place before any explanation. Across all judged posts, story is the most common hook type.
patterns.hypothesis: A concrete time and place lets the audience place themselves in the move before being asked to care about details.

patterns.title: Admin hurdles outperform scenery
patterns.observation: The clip whose first line names a visa or housing problem has the highest comment count relative to views.
patterns.hypothesis: Practical pain points invite questions, and questions drive comments.

clips.why_it_works: Opens on the first morning in the new flat, names the city, then cuts fast between three errands.
clips.hook_quote: Day one in Shanghai and I already got lost in my own compound.
clips.weaknesses: No on-screen text for the first six seconds.

clips.why_it_works: Curiosity gap in the first sentence, resolved only at the end.
clips.hook_quote: Nobody told me this about Shanghai supermarkets.
clips.weaknesses: Payoff arrives late for a 45-second clip.

gaps.title: Singlish and Mandarin code-switching
gaps.rationale: No shortlisted creator switches languages on camera, which the persona does naturally.

concepts.hook: I moved from Singapore to Shanghai with two suitcases. Here is what I bought on day one.
concepts.structure: 0-3s hook at the door; 3-20s three purchases with prices; 20-35s one surprise; 35-40s invite questions.
concepts.visual: Handheld, receipts held to camera, price overlays.
concepts.proof: Real receipts and the app screen.

concepts.hook: Three things my Singaporean brain refused to believe about Shanghai.
concepts.structure: 0-3s list promise; 3-30s three items, each with a clip; 30-40s which one changed my mind.
concepts.visual: Jump cuts, numbered overlays in English and Chinese.

caveats: Two of five fixture posts shortlisted; sample is illustrative only.
